brief.question: Is chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine effective for COVID-19 treatment, for which outcomes and populations?
brief.outcome: Evaluate the treatment claim without medical advice.
brief.scope: COVID-19 treatment; excludes approved non-COVID uses and prophylaxis.
brief.level_rationale: Medical claim with contested evidence and potential harm.

sources.author: Singh et al.
sources.title: Chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine for prevention and treatment of COVID-19

sources.author: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
sources.title: FDA Revokes Emergency Use Authorization for Chloroquine and Hydroxychloroquine

claims.statement: WHO guidance reports no treatment recommendation and no mortality or ventilation benefit in its reviewed trials.
Cochrane concluded hydroxychloroquine had little or no mortality effect and probably no ventilation benefit.
FDA revoked the EUA after finding the drugs unlikely to be effective for the authorized use.
For COVID-19 treatment, the reviewed evidence does not show clinically useful benefit outweighing relevant risks.

handoffs.work_performed: Separated treatment, prevention, efficacy, and regulatory evidence.
gaps: Primary-trial audit and full funding map pending.

handoffs.recommended_next_action: revalidate on material new controlled evidence

dossier.title: Chloroquine / hydroxychloroquine and COVID-19
dossier.conclusion: The evaluated synthesis and regulatory evidence does not support clinically useful COVID-19 treatment benefit; this excludes no approved non-COVID use.
dossier.confidence_rationale: Convergent synthesis and regulator record, with scope preserved.
